title.en: Slack cable engagement and tension-only coupling

summary: Move two cable endpoints and reveal the transition from slack to equal-and-opposite tensile forces.
objective: Expose the authoritative model and its visible response: slack cable engagement and tension-only coupling.
applies_when: An authored massless straight axial connector with fixed positive rest length, positive linear stiffness and zero damping; endpoint positions are prescribed for a force-response demonstration.
intent_signals: Move two cable endpoints and reveal the transition from slack to equal-and-opposite tensile forces.
example_prompts: Build an inspectable demonstration of slack cable engagement and tension-only coupling with parameter controls and a reset.
negative_signals: Not inextensible constraints, rope bending, distributed mass, pulley friction, dynamic catenaries or damping/rebound prediction.
not_for: Not inextensible constraints, rope bending, distributed mass, pulley friction, dynamic catenaries or damping/rebound prediction.

principles: A slack connector cannot push its endpoints apart. Prescribed endpoint movement and computed cable force must be identified separately.
This reduced element has no distributed sag state; a hanging curve is illustrative unless another model computes it.
implementation: Own positions A,B in m, rest length L0>0 in m and k>0 in N/m. Let d=|B-A| and extension e=d-L0. For e<=0 set tension and both forces to zero without normalizing a zero-length vector. For e>0 set n=(B-A)/d, T=k*e, FA=T*n, FB=-T*n.

Move a clamp with a position control and show the other endpoint plus opposing arrows and an extension readout. Use a straight taut segment; a slack glyph or explicitly illustrative curve should not masquerade as a catenary or collision-resolved rope.

Reset restores endpoints,L0,k and any display curve. If endpoints are later made dynamic, apply these forces to their authoritative masses and velocities with a separately documented integration/contact model; never move them both by a tween and a force solver.
observable_checks: For L0=1 m,k=100 N/m, d=0,0.8 or 1 m gives zero force; d=1.1 m gives 10 N directed toward the opposite endpoint.

Verify FA+FB=0 and T>=0; exchange endpoints and the force vectors exchange. Crossing the engagement length has continuous force with a slope change, without an undefined direction at coincident endpoints.

known_limits: Not inextensible constraints, rope bending, distributed mass, pulley friction, dynamic catenaries or damping/rebound prediction.
Authored reusable guidance; no solver or rendered artifact has been tested for this record.
creative_affordances: Use a cutaway, restrained ghost reference or annotated section only when it clarifies the modeled relation; a planar diagram remains valid when depth adds no information.

claims.statement: MathWorks Cable represents longitudinal tension transfer. Its zero-mass no-slack case is equivalent to a parallel spring and damper, while enabling slack removes stiffness and damping in the slack regime. The undamped unilateral endpoint law here is an explicitly authored reduced model, not a reproduction of all block options.
claims.scope: An authored massless straight axial connector with fixed positive rest length, positive linear stiffness and zero damping; endpoint positions are prescribed for a force-response demonstration.
